1. The order impugned vide this appeal is dated 10.01.2019 of Estate Officer vide which the Estate Officer has directed the appellant to recall the notice dated 17.07.2018 and to restore the lease of the property as per rules and regulations and thereafter issue fresh notice, if needed.
BRIEF FACTS 2.

The brief facts of the case as enumerated by the appellant are that the Delhi Improvement Trust being Lessor in PPA-01/2020 DDA Vs Sanjeev Kumar Aggarwal Page no. 1 of 17 the year 1947 had given the lease of the said land i.e. B-8, Block- 3, Rajinder Nagar Extension, New Delhi measuring 1000 sq. yds. (hereinafter referred to as 'the said land'), to custodian of the evacuee acting on behalf of one Sh. K.B vide the perpetual lease deed dated 24.10.1949.

The respondent had filed a civil suit claiming possession and recovery of damages in respect of the said land.

After inspection by the appellant of the said land, it is found that a school in the name and style of Multan DAV Sr.
Secondary School is being run on the said land in violation of the terms and purpose inked in the said perpetual lease deed.
The said land was leased for residential purpose only.
Since the said land was being used in violation of terms of the perpetual lease deed, it has been rightly determined by the Lessor/appellant on 22.12.2006 in accordance with law.

4. The civil suit was filed by the respondent for recovery of possession of the property and for recovery of mesne profit against Multan DAV Sr. Secondary School and DAV College Trust and Management Society.

the said land and against Multan DAV Sr. Secondary School.

Estate officer has overlooked the fact that the sale deed itself states that Appellant/DDA is the lessor.
In fact, it is the admitted case of respondent throughout the proceedings before the Court that the appellant is the lessor and the said land is the leasehold property.

It is submitted that Estate officer has miserably failed to appreciate that the said land has been PPA-01/2020 DDA Vs Sanjeev Kumar Aggarwal Page no. 5 of 17 transferred to various persons and further sub divided without any prior permission and is in clear violation of the terms of the original perpetual lease deed.

sentences.text: It is stated that admittedly, Multan DAV Society is in actual physical possession of the property and a school is being run there.

However, the respondent claims to have purchased the said land and he had filed a suit for possession against Multan DAV School seeking recovery of possession which was decided in his favour vide judgment and decree dated 21.12.2017.
It is stated that mutation of the property got canceled on 26.10.1995 which is prior to aforesaid purchase by the respondent.

It is further stated that Estate officer had issued a show cause notice dated 17.07.2018 u/s 4(1) of the PP Act to the respondent and he had appeared and filed his objections, but the Estate Officer has based the impugned order on the premise that before determining the lease the appellant has not issued notice to the respondent.

It is further stated that the Estate officer had in fact assumed the jurisdiction of Civil Court and had passed a decree of mandatory injunction by directing the appellant to restore the lease in favour of the respondent.
In support of his submissions Ld. Counsel has relied upon B.K. Bhagat Vs NDMC (supra).

Here, the Court has observed that apart from the functions and powers specially provided under the act, the Estate officer would not have any other powers, but he has passed several directions including renewal of the licence, which are clearly out of the scope of functions of the Court of Estate officer.

The Estate officer has no power to issue directions to the respondent to renew the licence, negotiate licence fee and/or direct the petitioner to withdraw its PPA-01/2020 DDA Vs Sanjeev Kumar Aggarwal Page no. 13 of 17 suit for specific performance.

sentences.text: In this suit, respondent had claimed to be the owner of the property on the strength of three sale deeds, all dated 28.08.2003, in his favour.

As already discussed, the said land was handed over to one K.B vide perpetual lease dated 24.10.1949 with specific condition that only residential building can be erected on the said land and the said land cannot be sub divided without consent of the lessor.

It further contains that lessee has to register all the changes in the possession of the whole of the said land or of the building thereon whether by transfer, succession or otherwise,
in the register kept in the office of the lessor for this purpose, within one calender month from the respective dates of such changes.

19. The most pertinent point to be considered is that as per the records of the appellant, the said land in question was mutated in favour of one Ms. Naseem Begum and Kamal Ahmad which was subsequently canceled vide the orders of the Collector dated 26.10.1995.
Then how respondent claim title over the said land on the basis of these three sale deeds all dated 28.08.2003.
The lease deed dated 24.10.1949 between appellant and said K.B is the most sacrosanct document and all terms and conditions settled between the two parties was required to be strictly adhered to.

There is nothing on record to assume if respondent got the rights of said land transferred in his favour subject to the compliance of the terms and conditions of this perpetual lease deed dated 24.10.1949.

sentences.text: As discussed earlier, the impugned order has been based on the premise that DDA is not challenging the ownership, but claiming the property by virtue of cancellation of lease deed due to misuse in the property.

As pointed out by Ld. Counsel for the respondent, appellant in its rejoinder to reply dated 17.12.2018 filed before the Estate officer has mentioned that- "DDA is not challenging the ownership but claiming the property by virtue of cancellation of lease deed due to misuse in the property.
After cancellation of sale deed, the occupier become unauthorized."

Certainly, as per perpetual lease deed of the said land, appellant could seek eviction on various ground including misuse of the property by not using for the purpose for which sanctioned and transfer of the property without mandatory permission of the lessor.
The point to be considered is that DDA is not challenging the ownership on the basis of the order of the Civil Court dated 21.12.2017 between respondent and DAV College Trust & Management Society.
As already discussed in this order, the Ld.ADJ has observed that the said land is owned by the respondent.
This is a judgment in personam between both the parties.

As the respondent was able to establish his better Delhi Development Authority vs Sanjeev Kumar Aggarwal on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75077602/
9 title of the said land, the Court passed order in his favour.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There, DDA was not a contesting party questioning ownership of the respondent, hence, judgment cannot be held to be binding regarding ownership of the property on the appellant.
It is a judgment which do not effect the legal status, but only determine the rights of the parties.
It is a judgment which is conclusive only against the parties to the suit.
Generally, all the judgments PPA-01/2020 DDA Vs Sanjeev Kumar Aggarwal Page no. 16 of 17 pronounced in the civil matters are judgments in personam.

sentences.text: 21. The other contention raised on behalf of the appellant is that the order is arbitrary and passed without application of mind and without considering the fact in accordance with Section 5 of the Act.
DECISION 22.

As per the impugned order, the Estate officer has only discussed the contention raised by the respondent that no notice was served on the respondent before cancellation of lease of the land in question, but it had not given any finding regarding service of notice to the respondent by the appellant.

Perusal of record of the Estate Officer revealed that respondent has filed reply dated 30.07.2018 to notice under Sub-Section (I) and clause (B)(II) of Sub-Section (2) of Section 4 of the PP Act, 1971.
23.
In view of the aforesaid reasons, I accept the appeal.
The impugned order is not sustainable and same is, accordingly set aside.
The Estate Officer is directed to proceed under Section 5 of the Act as expeditiously as possible.
24. Record of the Estate officer be sent back with a copy of this order.
Appeal file be consigned to record room.

Certainly, as per perpetual lease deed of the said land, appellant could seek eviction on various ground including misuse of the property by not using for the purpose for which sanctioned and transfer of the property without mandatory permission of the lessor.
The point to be considered is that DDA is not challenging the ownership on the basis of the order of the Civil Court dated 21.12.2017 between respondent and DAV College Trust & Management Society.
There, DDA was not a contesting party questioning ownership of the respondent, hence, judgment cannot be held to be binding regarding ownership of the property on the appellant.
It is a judgment which do not effect the legal status, but only determine the rights of the parties.
It is a judgment which is conclusive only against the parties to the suit.
